title: Declarative Rules
learning_objectives: Master declarative rule types and their applications
Learn to implement business logic without procedural code
Apply declarative patterns for maintainable solutions

introduction.title: Declarative Rules in PEGA
introduction.text: Declarative rules represent one of PEGA's most powerful features, allowing you to express business logic in a declarative manner rather than procedural code. These rules automatically execute when their dependencies change, providing reactive and maintainable business logic implementation.

sections.title: Types of Declarative Rules
sections.content: PEGA provides several types of declarative rules, each serving specific business logic needs.

rule_types.description: Enforce business rules and data integrity requirements
characteristics: Execute automatically when dependent properties change
use_cases: Data validation (email format, date ranges, numeric limits)
Business rule enforcement (credit limits, approval thresholds)
Cross-field validations (start date before end date)
Conditional requirements (required fields based on other selections)

example.rule: Credit limit cannot exceed customer's annual income
example.message: Credit limit cannot exceed annual income of $X

rule_types.description: Calculate derived values automatically based on other properties
characteristics: Forward chaining - recalculate when dependencies change
Support complex mathematical and logical operations
use_cases: Derived status values (case priority, risk scores)

example.rule: Calculate total order amount including tax

rule_types.description: Execute activities when specific property changes occur
characteristics: Can call activities, flows, or other processing
Support conditional execution based on property values
use_cases: Audit logging when sensitive data changes
Notification sending when status updates occur
Integration calls when key properties are modified
Workflow initiation based on data changes

example.rule: Send notification when case status changes to 'Resolved'

rule_types.description: Execute logic immediately when specific properties change
characteristics: Can modify other properties in response
Support cascading changes across multiple properties
use_cases: Auto-populate related fields based on selections
Dynamic UI updates based on user input

example.rule: Auto-populate city and state when ZIP code changes

summary.title: Key Takeaways
points: Declarative rules provide powerful reactive programming capabilities in PEGA
Different rule types serve specific purposes: constraints for validation, expressions for calculations, triggers for events
Advanced patterns enable sophisticated business logic implementation without procedural code
Proper dependency management and performance optimization are crucial for scalable solutions
Integration with procedural rules requires careful design and clear boundaries
Comprehensive testing ensures reliable declarative rule behavior
Following best practices leads to maintainable and performant declarative solutions
